articles.title: In 1996, rookie Derek Jeter and his father started a foundation to steer young people away from drugs and alcohol; 30 years later, Turn 2 has given more than $48 million and one of its programmes has reached over 30,000 students, families and school staff
articles.summary: Long before Derek Jeter became one of baseball's biggest names, he was already thinking about what his success could mean away from the diamond.
articles.body: Long before Derek Jeter became one of baseball's biggest names, he was already thinking about what his success could mean away from the diamond. During his rookie season in 1996, Jeter and his father, Dr. Charles Jeter, created the Turn 2 Foundation with a simple goal: encourage young people to avoid drugs and alcohol while making healthier choices. Three decades later, that idea has grown into a major charitable legacy. Turn 2 says it has given back more than $48 million, while its Turn 2 Us programme alone has reached more than 30,000 students, families and school staff.Derek Jeter launched Turn 2 during his rookie seasonJeter's first full year in Major League Baseball quickly changed his life. The New York Yankees shortstop won the American League Rookie of the Year award in 1996 and helped the club win the World Series. But while his baseball career was taking off, another project was beginning outside the stadium.Jeter and his father had discussed ways to use his growing platform to help young people. That conversation eventually became the Turn 2 Foundation.The organisation was built around prevention and opportunity. Its early work focused on helping young people make positive decisions, stay away from substance abuse and develop habits that could put them on a better path. The foundation also placed a strong emphasis on education, leadership and personal development.The timing was significant. Jeter was still establishing himself as a professional athlete, yet he chose to make community work part of his identity from the beginning.That decision became a foundation of his life away from baseball.Turn 2 grew from a small idea into a major charityThe early days of Turn 2 were far less polished than the organisation is today. Jeter's first fundraising efforts were relatively modest, with an event in Kalamazoo, Michigan, raising tens of thousands of dollars.But the foundation kept growing as Jeter's career developed.Turn 2 expanded its programmes and partnerships, targeting communities where young people could benefit from extra support. Rather than focusing on one issue, the organisation developed a wider approach that included education, healthy lifestyles, leadership and career development.That broader mission helped Turn 2 remain relevant long after Jeter's playing career ended.According to the foundation's current figures, Turn 2 has now given back more than $48 million over its 30-year history. The organisation's work extends across communities in New York, Michigan and Florida, among other areas.The number is striking because Turn 2 did not begin with the resources of a major national charity. It started with a young baseball player, his father and a desire to help teenagers make better choices.Three decades later, that small beginning has become one of the most lasting parts of Jeter's legacy.Derek Jeter’s Turn 2 Us programme has reached 30,000 peopleOne of Turn 2's most notable initiatives is the Turn 2 Us programme, which demonstrates how the foundation moved from a broad mission to hands-on community work.The programme began in 2001 through a partnership involving Turn 2, NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital and Public School 128M in Washington Heights. Its focus was on helping children and the adults around them develop healthier habits and stronger support systems.The programme has since expanded to additional elementary schools.According to MLB's Turn 2 Foundation page, Turn 2 Us has served more than 30,000 students, school staff and families in Northern Manhattan and surrounding communities.That reach is important because the programme does not treat students as isolated individuals. Schools are communities, and children are influenced by teachers, parents and other adults around them.By involving students, families and school staff, Turn 2 Us creates a wider network of support.The programme also reflects the foundation's original philosophy. Prevention is not simply about telling young people what not to do. It is about giving them useful alternatives, trusted adults and opportunities to build confidence.For a foundation that began with a goal of steering young people away from drugs and alcohol, that approach has allowed the mission to evolve without losing its original purpose.Derek Jeter’s legacy extends beyond his Yankees careerJeter's baseball résumé is already enough to secure his place in sports history. He spent his entire 20-year MLB career with the Yankees, collected five World Series titles and finished with more than 3,400 hits. He was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2020.Yet Turn 2 represents a different kind of record.There is no batting average attached to a foundation. No championship ring measures the effect of helping a teenager develop healthier habits or giving a family access to support. The impact can be harder to see, but it can last much longer.That is particularly clear when looking at how Turn 2 has developed over 30 years.Jeter's transition from a rookie baseball player to a retired superstar did not end his connection with the organisation. Instead, Turn 2 continued building programmes around the same themes that inspired its creation.The foundation now focuses on helping young people pursue education, healthy lifestyles and leadership opportunities. It also supports programmes designed to strengthen families and communities.The $48 million figure tells only part of the story. The more personal measure may be the number of people who encountered Turn 2 through a school, community programme or educational initiative.For Jeter, the project began at a moment when his own future was still uncertain. He was a rookie trying to establish himself in the majors. Thirty years later, his baseball career is over, but the organisation he started with his father continues to work with young people.That may be the most meaningful part of the Turn 2 story.Jeter entered the Yankees clubhouse as a promising 22-year-old and eventually became one of baseball's most recognisable figures. But while the statistics tell the story of his career on the field, Turn 2 offers another set of numbers: more than $48 million given back and more than 30,000 people reached through Turn 2 Us.The foundation's story shows how a decision made during a rookie season can outlast a playing career by decades. articles.title: MLB Draft Lottery 2027 Odds Revealed for Mets, More After Regular Season Ends
articles.summary: The New York Mets may have fallen massively short of expectations in 2026, but at least they have a chance to replenish their farm system in next year's draft.
articles.body:
The New York Mets may have fallen massively short of expectations in 2026, but at least they have a chance to replenish their farm system in next year's draft.

The Colorado Rockies, Los Angeles Angels and Athletics are the three teams at the top of the lottery odds. They have a 19.1 percent chance of landing the No. 1 overall pick and are 87.6 percent on for staying in the top six.

The Mets are long shots for the first pick but should at least hang around the top six:

The 2026 draft opened with a pair of shortstops: UCLA's Roch Cholowsky and prep prospect Grady Emerson. Next year could be a similar story.

In his early projections for 2027, MLB.com's Jonathan Mayo led off with high schooler Dylan Seward and Florida star Brendan Lawson. Joel Reuter of Bleacher Report mocked Seward at No. 2 behind Mississippi State pitcher Tomas Valincius. Lawson went fourth overall.

Reuter called Seward "a quick-twitch athlete with top-of-the-scale speed, advanced bat-to-ball skills and elite bat speed to generate some playable power even with a 6'0", 175-pound frame."

Whoever lands the No. 1 pick may prefer a more polished prospect, much as the White Sox did with Cholowsky.

Lawson had a .511 on-base percentage and slugged .699 with the Gators in 2026. His homer total nearly doubled, going from 10 as a freshman to 19.

Valincius, who transferred to the Bulldogs from Virginia, went 11-2 with a 3.50 ERA in 17 starts. He struck out 134 batters in 97.2 innings. More of the same in 2027 will make him the best pitcher in the class.
